result:
**Rebuttal from debater B**

Debater A and I agree on the arithmetic and on the orders p − 1, p^{n−1}, and p^{n−1}(p − 1). The disagreement is about which subgroups qualify, and A has not shown that the three listed are the only ones that work.

A's justification is that these are "the natural candidates given the cyclic structure of Aut(G)." Naturalness is not a classification. Aut(G) is cyclic, so it has one subgroup for each divisor of p^{n−1}(p − 1), and there are many more than three such divisors in general. A has not explained why the qualifying subgroups must be the Sylow p-subgroup, its complement, and the whole group, rather than some other subgroups of that cyclic group.

The claim that these three subgroups give almost commutative Terwilliger algebras comes from the solution, not from a derivation either debater has given. A cites no theorem and offers no check. I have not verified it independently either.

So the sum p^n + p − 1 is correct only if the classification is correct. Neither debater has shown that it is, so the judge should not treat A's "natural candidates" as settling the question.
